svg.title: The airspeed correction chain from indicated to true airspeed

desc.style: color: rgb(34, 48, 63); fill: rgb(0, 0, 0); fill-opacity: 1; fill-rule: nonzero; stroke: none; stroke-width: 1px; stroke-opacity: 1; stroke-dasharray: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-linejoin: miter; opacity: 1; font-size: 17px; font-family: Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; text-anchor: start; dominant-baseline: auto; letter-spacing: normal; visibility: visible; paint-order: normal; marker: none;

svg.desc: Indicated airspeed is corrected for instrument error and pressure or position error to give calibrated airspeed. From calibrated airspeed there are two paths. At low speed, correcting density error alone gives true airspeed directly. At high speed, correcting compressibility first gives equivalent airspeed, and then correcting density error gives true airspeed. The dividing line is 300 knots true airspeed.
